clue.text: After poor score, Lord's protecting new batsman

indicators.note: the Lord's letters are placed after the poor score in the answer

parts.note: a duck, nought runs in cricket, is written as the letter O

indicators.note: the peer's letters surround and guard the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a new batsman coming in at Lord's after a dismal score.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, which steers the reader to cricket; here it is just a peer. The opener is the batsman who starts an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: The batsman who begins an innings for a cricket side is called by this name.

clue.text: Agree in court to pay costs

definitions.meaning: to agree a case in court is to settle it
paying what is owed settles the account

explanation.surface: A litigant settles a case and agrees to cover the expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to settle, whether a dispute or a debt owed to someone.

clue.text: Conflict with so-called enemy power in which there's no rotated progress

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Conflict with so-called enemy power in which there's no rotated progress'. TIME (the old enemy) + WAR + P (power) builds the answer, but 'rotated' makes no sense in the definition and looks misread; no source gives the printed word.
annotationWithheld.clue: Conflict with so-called enemy power in which there's no rotated progress

clue.text: Consider what boxing fan wants to do?

definitions.meaning: to consider a matter is to attend to it or look into it

definitions.text: what boxing fan wants to do?
definitions.meaning: a fan of boxing wants to watch a fight, to see a contest in the ring

explanation.surface: A boxing enthusiast weighs up going to a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To see about something is to deal with it or think it over.

clue.text: Be good at posing as member of 6 literary family

parts.note: an artist's model who is good at posing does it well: sit plus well
doing a thing well means being good at it

explanation.surface: A society portrait sitter is praised for holding a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '6' is most likely an OCR slip for 'a'. Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell Sitwell were a famous English literary family of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell, poet, and her brothers Osbert and Sacheverell were all writers, the best-known literary siblings of their day.

clue.text: Central Revolutionary car developed in China after revolution

clue.text: Frequently ring newspapers

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
FT is the Financial Times, a London daily
The Times is another London daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone telephones the press over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Two newspapers, the FT and The Times, come out of the one plural word. 'Ring' looks like a phone call but it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft-times is an old poetic word for often, many times over.

clue.text: Actor, having done this, is savagely reviewed

definitions.meaning: an actor who has accepted a role has ...
harsh critics demolish, or tear to pieces, the work they review

explanation.surface: A performer who has played a role gets slated by the critics.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that critics tear to pieces has been demolished in print; an actor who has played a role has accepted it.

clue.text: Send journalist in to make a new proposal

indicators.note: the journalist is placed inside the word for send

parts.note: to remit is to send, as money by post
a sub is a subeditor, a newspaper journalist who checks copy

explanation.surface: An editor dispatches a reporter to pitch a fresh scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit again is to put forward a proposal a second time.

clue.text: Composer's skill concealed by half-hearted libretto

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the skill is hidden inside the shortened word for libretto
one of the two letters in the heart of the libretto word is dropped

parts.note: the book of an opera or musical is its libretto, its words
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A composer's talent is hidden by a feeble opera text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the two letters at the centre of the libretto word, leaving BOK. Bela Bartok was a Hungarian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Bartok was the twentieth-century Hungarian composer of the Concerto for Orchestra.

clue.text: Notice changed on royal building

indicators.note: the rearranged notice letters are placed on, that is after, the royal letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

indicators.note: the letters of notice are changed around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A notice on a royal palace has been altered.
explanation.definitionFit: An erection is a structure that has been put up, such as a building.

clue.text: Take a drop before opening time

definitions.text: Take a drop before opening time

parts.words: Take a drop before opening time
parts.note: reads like having a drink before the pub opens, but describes a skydiver dropping before the parachute opens

explanation.surface: A drinker sneaks a tipple before the pub opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver's plunge before pulling the ripcord is the unchecked descent of a body under gravity.

clue.text: Lots of keen, excited, foreign travellers here?

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Crowds of eager, thrilled foreign tourists arrive at some spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Folkestone is a Kent port on the English Channel, where travellers from the Continent come ashore; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: As a Channel port and Tunnel terminal, this Kent town is where many visitors from abroad arrive.

clue.text: Old man's driven vehicle over river

indicators.note: the old man is driven around inside the vehicle, so his letters go within it

parts.note: a limo is a limousine, a chauffeured car
pop is a familiar word for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: Someone's father has driven his car over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Limpopo is a river of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limpopo flows through southern Africa into the Indian Ocean, famously 'great grey-green' in Kipling.

clue.text: Plant tree, giving protection to, bark

indicators.note: the tree word wraps itself round the bark word, sheltering it

parts.note: the maple is a tree, as in the sugar maple
to yap is to bark shrilly, like a small dog

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a tree that shields the trunk's bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' looks like part of the tree but it is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The may apple is a North American woodland plant with a single large white flower.

clue.text: Conservative party members getting on with defence

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old
a guard is a defence, as in a fire guard

explanation.surface: Elderly Tory activists are getting ready to defend themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The old guard are the long-standing members of a group who resist change.

clue.text: Wife and mother in complex relationship

definitions.text: Wife and mother in complex relationship

parts.words: Wife and mother in complex relationship
parts.note: reads as a tangled family drama, but points to the Greek queen of Thebes who wed her own son, the source of the Oedipus complex

explanation.surface: A woman is both spouse and parent in a tangled family situation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the queen of Thebes unknowingly married her son Oedipus, being both his wife and his mother.

clue.text: Later on I moved from India to the Philippines

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a different order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A traveller later relocated from India to the Philippines.
explanation.definitionFit: Asian lands lying east of Europe, India to the Philippines, were once called the Orient.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, I had a chance

indicators.note: the contraction for I had goes in the manner of speaking

parts.note: an accent is a way of pronouncing words
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone says that, as it were, they had an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like the stock phrase meaning 'so to speak', but it splits: 'In' is the insertion signal and 'a manner of speaking' is ACCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening by chance, unplanned, happens by accident.

clue.text: Rising diver caught one cold fish

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down clue the diver word goes upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A diver comes up having caught a single fish in cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' is a bird, not a swimmer; 'cold fish' is the definition, an unemotional person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is emotionally frozen and aloof is called a cold fish, or an iceberg.

clue.text: Couple featuring in spiteful woman's gossip

indicators.note: the couple word appears inside the spiteful woman word

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful, malicious woman
to hitch is to couple, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: A malicious woman passes on tittle-tattle about a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a pair of people but it is a verb, to link up.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit-chat is light, idle talk, much like gossip.

clue.text: American capital for Englishman making cars

definitions.meaning: the capital city of the state of Texas
Herbert ... founded the British motor company that bore his name

explanation.surface: An American city is named for a British motor manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin is the state capital of Texas, and Herbert Austin founded a famous British car maker.

clue.text: Daydream, as 'showbiz fans are wont to do?

definitions.meaning: to daydream is to be lost in idle thoughts

definitions.text: as 'showbiz fans are wont to do?
definitions.meaning: fans of show business gaze at celebrities, the stars

explanation.surface: Celebrity fans let their minds wander while gawping at celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: To stargaze is to daydream, and literally to gaze at stars, as celebrity fans do.

clue.text: Issue to be raised when parents are late

definitions.text: Issue to be raised when parents are late

parts.words: Issue to be raised when parents are late
parts.note: reads like a complaint about tardy parents, but issue means a child and late means dead

explanation.surface: A school complains about parents arriving late to collect children.
explanation.definitionFit: A child whose mother and father have died is left without parents to bring it up.

clue.text: Request access to have a meal inside

indicators.note: the meal word goes inside the access word

parts.note: entry is access, a way in
to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be let in for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or request.

clue.text: Making revisions, the writer rejected denouement

indicators.note: the writer word is thrown back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me
a denouement is the ending of a story

explanation.surface: An author revises a manuscript after an editor turns down its conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or revise it.

clue.text: Overdue books in existence, but not yet out

definitions.text: in existence, but not yet out

parts.note: something overdue is late
NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Library books are overdue; they exist but have not yet come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but hidden, not yet developed or visible.
